title: Temporary files older than a week
explain: Files programs left in your temporary folder and have not touched for a week. Programs that still need theirs keep them in use, and those are skipped.

title: Browser caches
explain: Copies of web pages and scripts Chrome, Edge or Firefox saved to load sites faster. The browser downloads them again as you browse; close it first so nothing is in use.

title: Old installers in Downloads
explain: Setup programs downloaded more than 90 days ago. Once a program is installed its installer is usually not needed, and most can be downloaded again.

title: Crash dumps
explain: Memory snapshots Windows saved when a program crashed. They only help a developer investigating that crash.

title: Windows error reports
explain: Problem reports Windows collected about crashed programs, already sent or queued. Windows creates new ones if a program crashes again.

title: Thumbnail cache
explain: Picture previews File Explorer saved. Explorer redraws them as you browse folders; files it is using right now are skipped.

title: npm package cache
explain: Every package npm has downloaded. npm fetches what a project needs again on its next install.

title: pip download cache
explain: Python packages pip downloaded or built. pip downloads them again when they are next installed.

title: Cargo registry cache
explain: Rust crates Cargo downloaded, with their index. Cargo downloads what a project needs on its next build.

title: NuGet package folder
explain: Every .NET package NuGet has restored. dotnet restore downloads what a project needs again.

title: Windows temporary files
explain: Temporary files Windows itself keeps. StorageLens does not change anything inside the Windows folder; Disk Cleanup removes these safely as an administrator.

title: Windows Update downloads
explain: Update files Windows downloaded and has usually already installed. In Disk Cleanup, choose Clean up system files and then Windows Update Cleanup.

title: Delivery Optimization cache
explain: Update pieces Windows keeps to share with other PCs. Run the command in PowerShell as an administrator to clear it; Windows downloads again what it needs.

title: Previous Windows installation
explain: The previous version of Windows, kept after an upgrade so you can go back. In Disk Cleanup, choose Clean up system files and then Previous Windows installation; after that you can no longer roll back.

title: Items in the Recycle Bin
explain: Files already in the Recycle Bin still take space until it is emptied. Empty it when you are sure; StorageLens never does, because that is what makes its own deletions undoable.

title: Hibernation file
explain: Where Windows saves memory to hibernate and to start up faster. Turning hibernation off in an administrator prompt removes it; Fast Startup stops working too.

title: Page file
explain: Virtual memory, managed by Windows. Its size can be changed under Advanced, then Virtual memory, in the window this command opens; removing it can make programs fail.

title: Windows component store
explain: Windows' own components and the earlier versions updates replaced. Much of its apparent size is shared with the Windows folder; running the command as an administrator removes superseded versions.
